summary: Bumps @cipherstash/auth 0.40->0.41 (Result-returning API) and @cipherstash/protect-ffi 0.27->0.28, migrates the CLI, wizard and the stack WASM access-key path to unwrap Results, and renames the re-exported AuthError type to AuthFailure. The internal call-site migrations look consistent and the WASM access-key path is covered by unit tests plus a live Deno round-trip in CI. The main release risk is to consumers of @cipherstash/stack (a 0.x minor): the strategy constructors it re-exports (AccessKeyStrategy/OidcFederationStrategy .create) now return Result envelopes, yet the package's own JSDoc examples and the live lock-context test still pass `.create(...)` directly as `authStrategy`, so code written that way breaks after upgrade. Separately, whether protect-ffi 0.28's native (Node) newClient unwraps the new getToken() Result envelope is not shown anywhere: the changeset only claims the WASM newClient does, and the only live test of a real auth strategy on the native path is gated on USER_JWT, which CI does not provide. Identity-bound (OIDC) encryption on Node is the path most exposed. Failures would be loud (init or ZeroKMS request errors), not silent data issues.

behaviour_changes.description: @cipherstash/stack re-exports auth strategies from @cipherstash/auth (native entry and wasm-inline entry). With auth 0.41, their constructors (AccessKeyStrategy.create, OidcFederationStrategy.create, AutoStrategy.detect, DeviceSessionStrategy.fromProfile) and getToken() return `{ data } | { failure }` instead of the strategy/token or throwing. The re-export code is unchanged, so the public behaviour of these stack exports changes with the dependency bump.
The type re-export `AuthError` from @cipherstash/stack is removed and replaced by `AuthFailure` (a discriminated union keyed by `type`). Consumers importing AuthError no longer compile.
WASM-inline resolveStrategy now unwraps AccessKeyStrategy.create's Result and throws a descriptive `[encryption]: failed to construct AccessKeyStrategy ... (<type>): <message>` error on failure.

protect-ffi pinned 0.27.0 -> 0.28.0; the changeset states 0.28's WASM newClient reads `.data.token` from getToken()'s Result envelope. Native newClient behaviour with the envelope (and with plain `{ token }` custom strategies) is not described.

CLI (`stash auth login`, device binding, init auth check) and wizard (token acquisition, prompt fetch, prerequisites check) switch from try/catch and `error.code` to `result.failure` / `failure.type`. Wizard hasCredentials treats failure.type NOT_AUTHENTICATED or MISSING_WORKSPACE_CRN as 'no credentials' and rethrows failure.error otherwise.

The Deno WASM e2e now imports auth and protect-ffi WASM entries from file paths inside packages/stack/node_modules instead of pinned npm: specifiers (previously protect-ffi 0.26.0 and auth 0.40.0), so the e2e tests the versions stack actually installs.

failure_scenarios.title: Strategy constructors re-exported by @cipherstash/stack now return Result; documented `authStrategy: X.create(...)` usage breaks on upgrade
failure_scenarios.trigger: A consumer (or the repo's own lock-context test) passes `AccessKeyStrategy.create(...)` or `OidcFederationStrategy.create(...)` directly as `config.authStrategy`, as the package's JSDoc examples show, then upgrades to the new @cipherstash/stack minor.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: auth 0.41 `create` returns `{ data } | { failure }` (changeset line 9; resolveStrategy now unwraps it at wasm-inline.ts:474-480). @cipherstash/stack re-exports these constructors unchanged (index.ts:26-36), and its JSDoc still shows `authStrategy: AccessKeyStrategy.create(workspaceCrn, accessKey)` and `OidcFederationStrategy.create(...)` passed straight through (encryption/index.ts:756-781, identity/index.ts:64-74, wasm-inline.ts:44-56). Encryption forwards config.authStrategy verbatim to newClient (encryption/index.ts:166), so the Result envelope, which has no getToken, reaches protect-ffi. The in-repo live test lock-context.test.ts:38-45 does the same and was not updated.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Client init or the first ZeroKMS request fails for every app that builds its strategy this way, including identity-bound (lock-context) encryption. TypeScript users likely get a compile error; JS users get a runtime failure. Encryption on that path is unavailable until code is changed. The changeset lists only the AuthError rename as the stack breaking surface, so users are not warned.

failure_scenarios.title: Native-path protect-ffi 0.28 handling of the getToken() Result envelope is unverified
failure_scenarios.trigger: A Node (native entry) user supplies a real auth 0.41 strategy (e.g. an unwrapped OidcFederationStrategy for lock context) or a custom `{ getToken: async () => ({ token }) }` strategy as config.authStrategy.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: Under auth 0.41 every strategy's getToken() returns `Result<TokenResult, AuthFailure>`. The changeset says protect-ffi 0.28 unwraps `.data.token` inside its WASM newClient and that 0.27 failed with `token field is not a string`; it says nothing about the native newClient. The stack still documents the AuthStrategy contract as `getToken(): Promise<{ token: string }>` (types.ts:21-31) and its unit test uses that shape with a mocked newClient (init-strategy.test.ts:49-58). If native 0.28 reads `.token`, real auth strategies fail on every ZeroKMS request; if it requires `.data.token`, custom `{ token }` strategies documented as supported break.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Explicit-strategy encryption/decryption on Node fails (loudly) for one of the two strategy shapes. Identity-bound encryption with OidcFederationStrategy on Node is the most exposed path. Default env/profile credentials (no authStrategy) are not affected by this mechanism.

failure_scenarios.title: Wizard prerequisites check may throw instead of reporting missing credentials if auth 0.41 failure.type strings differ
failure_scenarios.trigger: A user without credentials runs the wizard and auth 0.41 reports the condition with a type other than 'NOT_AUTHENTICATED' or 'MISSING_WORKSPACE_CRN'.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: hasCredentials (prerequisites.ts:45-58) compares failure.type to the old error.code strings, typed as plain `string`, so a renamed variant is not caught at compile time. The stack's own test uses a PascalCase failure type ('InvalidWorkspaceCrn', wasm-inline-strategy.test.ts:79), so not every 0.41 type follows the old SCREAMING_CASE names. The mocked wizard test only covers the NOT_AUTHENTICATED case.
failure_scenarios.consequence: The wizard aborts with a raw auth error instead of listing 'missing credentials' guidance. Local, recoverable.

evidence.claim: Changeset states auth 0.41 constructors and getToken return Result, AuthError is renamed to AuthFailure, and protect-ffi 0.28 unwraps the envelope in its WASM newClient (native newClient not mentioned).
@cipherstash/stack re-exports AccessKeyStrategy, AutoStrategy, DeviceSessionStrategy and OidcFederationStrategy straight from @cipherstash/auth.

JSDoc examples pass `AccessKeyStrategy.create(workspaceCrn, accessKey)` and `OidcFederationStrategy.create(...)` directly as authStrategy; same pattern in identity/index.ts:64-74 and wasm-inline.ts:44-56. Not updated by this change.
Type re-export now lists AuthErrorCode, AuthFailure, TokenResult; AuthError removed.
resolveStrategy unwraps AccessKeyStrategy.create's Result and throws on failure.
Native Encryption forwards config.authStrategy unchanged to protect-ffi newClient as `strategy`.
Unit test uses a `{ getToken: async () => ({ token }) }` strategy with a mocked newClient; it checks forwarding only.
CLI device-code flow and bindDevice unwrap Results and exit on failure.
hasCredentials returns false for failure.type NOT_AUTHENTICATED / MISSING_WORKSPACE_CRN and rethrows otherwise; predicate typed as `{ type: string }`.
Deno import map now resolves auth/protect-ffi WASM entries from packages/stack/node_modules instead of npm: pins.
Live test passes `OidcFederationStrategy.create(crn, ...)` directly as authStrategy without unwrapping the Result; skips when USER_JWT is absent.
New test covers the resolveStrategy failure arm using a mocked failure of type 'InvalidWorkspaceCrn'.
CI runs the Deno WASM smoke test (live access-key round-trip) after building stack.
Re-export test checks only that each strategy is a defined function identical to the auth binding.
CI writes CS_* credentials for packages/stack tests but no USER_JWT; no workflow references USER_JWT.
AuthStrategy contract documented as any object with `getToken(): Promise<{ token: string }>`; not updated for the Result envelope.
